To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified three new heterozygous postzogotic mutations in the PIK3CA gene in three PROS patients and that these mutations result in constitutive activation of AKT and mTOR signaling, suggesting that inhibition PI3K might be beneficial in PROS patients.
we found three different postzygotic mutations in PIK3R1, PIK3CA, and AKT1 genes in three patients affected by different PROS disorders.
the PI3K inhibitor wortmannin reduced the growth of dermal fibroblast from PROS patients, indicating that PI3K might represent a potential target for future therapies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular defects in patients with PROS.
the identification of molecular mechanisms underlying PROS pathogenesis and the development of novel therapies.
the molecular characterization of three different postzygotic mutations in PROS patients, and with the effects of these mutations on PI3K signaling pathway and sensitivity to PI3K inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PROS patients are characterized by a constitutive activation of PI3K/AKt/mTOR pathway that can be effectively blocked by pharmacological inhibitors.
PROS syndromes represent a unique opportunity to study the role of the PI3k/Akt/mTor pathway in the development of human tissues.
the molecular mechanisms underlying PROS are complex and multifactorial, but that PI3K/AkT pathway activation is a common denominator in all PROS subgroups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the genetic cause of the disease and we showed that pharmacological targeting of the PI3k/AKT pathway might be an effective therapeutic approach.
PIK3CA is a good target for the treatment of PROS patients.
we found that PI3K inhibition could be a potential treatment for PROS patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of the molecular defect underlying PROS syndromes is crucial to provide a diagnosis and to guide the therapeutic approach.
PI3K inhibitors may have therapeutic value for PROS patients, and we suggest that the use of these drugs should be considered for PROS patients with PIK3CA somatic mutations.

the identification of causative mutations and the characterization of their effects on signaling and sensitivity to pharmacologic agents might help to develop a more personalized approach for PROS treatment.
